stem: A client has persistent basophilia on repeated complete blood counts. Which statement by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Basophilia is nonspecific; persistent elevation warrants clinical and hematologic evaluation because causes include inflammatory, hypersensitivity, infectious, and myeloproliferative disorders.
options.B: Persistent basophilia is generally a benign normal variant, so repeated elevation does not require correlation with symptoms or other CBC findings.
options.C: Basophilia establishes acute bacterial infection and should be interpreted as a disease-specific marker without considering other hematologic abnormalities.
options.D: Basophilia identifies a single allergic disorder, so persistent elevation can be attributed to hypersensitivity without evaluating alternative causes.

rationale: Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance describes basophilia as a nonspecific finding associated with hypersensitivity and inflammatory reactions, infections, and myeloproliferative disorders including CML. The June 2026 Leukocytosis review states that persistent basophilia on serial CBCs raises concern for an underlying malignancy or myeloproliferative disorder, whereas transient basophilia can be reactive. Therefore persistent basophilia requires interpretation with the full clinical and hematologic context. A is correct; B, C, and D each make an unsupported disease-specific or dismissive conclusion.
educational_objective: Interpret persistent basophilia as a nonspecific finding that warrants clinical and hematologic evaluation for reactive and clonal causes.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
source_version_date: Basophilia last update August 11, 2024, StatPearls 2026 edition; Leukocytosis last update June 15, 2026; live NCBI pages retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Basophilia Etiology/Histopathology: causes include allergic/hypersensitivity reactions, chronic inflammation/infection, and myeloproliferative neoplasms; basophilia is usually nonspecific. Leukocytosis Basophilia section: persistent basophilia on serial CBCs raises concern for malignancy/myeloproliferative disorder.
source_claim_supported: Basophilia is nonspecific and may be reactive or clonal; persistent basophilia warrants evaluation in clinical and hematologic context.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory findings and recognize abnormal trends.
correction_summary: Removed 'always/never' cueing and balanced all options as parallel interpretations of persistent basophilia.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current NCBI evidence explicitly supports multiple reactive/clonal causes and evaluation of persistent basophilia; A uniquely matches.
